# Dimension: How the Agent Consumes LLMs

How Hermes Agent talks to a model. Sources in [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Model is decoupled — Hermes is a harness, not a model

Hermes Agent is provider-agnostic: it brings the agent loop, tools, and memory, and
calls **any** chat model over a provider abstraction. You "switch models without code
changes" [5]. It does **not** ship with a bundled model; Nous Research's own Hermes 4
(70B/405B) is available but **not recommended** for the agent's tool-calling loop —
those weights are tuned for chat/reasoning. Docs steer you to frontier agentic models
(e.g. Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.5 Pro, Gemini 3 Pro) [3].

## How a request flows

1. A frontend (or messaging platform) sends a prompt to Hermes' OpenAI-compatible
   server [4].
2. Hermes runs its agent loop, deciding tool calls (terminal/file/web/memory/skills),
   and for each LLM turn issues a chat/responses call to the **configured provider** [4].
3. The provider is selected by `--provider` / `config.yaml`; credentials live in
   `~/.hermes/.env` or `~/.hermes/auth.json` [2][3].

## Provider classes (from the provider matrix [2])

| Class | Examples | Auth | Note |
|-------|----------|------|------|
| Cloud API (direct) | Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, GitHub Copilot | API key / OAuth | Claude has 3 auth modes — see [billing-subscription-vs-api.md](billing-subscription-vs-api.md) |
| Aggregators / routers | OpenRouter (FAQ-recommended), LiteLLM, ClawRouter | Single API key | One key → hundreds of models [6] |
| Nous Portal | 300+ models incl. Claude, GPT, Gemini, Hermes | **OAuth + one credit balance** | Vendor-recommended gateway [3] |
| Enterprise cloud | AWS Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry | Cloud creds | Bedrock uses boto3 chain, no API key [2] |
| Self-hosted / local | vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio | none / local | Must expose OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` [2] |

## Tool-calling requirement

Because the agent leans on a rapid tool-call loop, the served model must support
function/tool calling. For self-hosted backends this means explicit flags, e.g. vLLM
`--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`, SGLang `--tool-call-parser`,
llama.cpp `--jinja` [2]. Models with native tool-calling called out: Llama 3.x,
Qwen 2.5, Hermes 2/3, Mistral, DeepSeek, Functionary; Claude and Grok 4 support
"automatic reasoning" via the Responses API transport [2].

## Implication for the billing question

Because the model is pluggable, **the cost model is entirely the provider's** [6]. The
agent adds no LLM markup. The "can I use a Claude subscription" question is therefore a
question about the **Anthropic provider path**, not about Hermes — see
[billing-subscription-vs-api.md](billing-subscription-vs-api.md).

## Self-hosted-model escape hatch

Pointing Hermes at a local vLLM/SGLang/Ollama endpoint removes per-token LLM cost
entirely — "local models incur no costs" [6] — at the price of running inference
hardware. This is the natural pairing with a k3s + GPU cluster (see
[k3s-openshell-sandboxing.md](k3s-openshell-sandboxing.md)).

## Gaps and Limitations

- Nous Portal's exact per-token / credit pricing is **not published** on the fetched
  page [3]; only "one credit balance" is stated.
- Whether NemoClaw's "routed inference" supplies its own managed model or only proxies
  external providers is **not specified** in the fetched README [10].
